thread.title: Apple Pivots Its Business Model - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)

author: Michael Wiggins De Oliveira
title: Apple Pivots Its Business Model - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)
text:
Investment Thesis Apple ( AAPL ) is by far my favorite investment, at present, amongst all mega-cap tech stocks (and I know many). Every single aspect of this investment makes sense, from the adaptation to a superior business model, driven by strong recurring revenue, to what I believe carries the most weight, its present valuation, as investors become uninterested in Apple.
Creates An Annuity Apple amassed unparalleled success with the iPhone. This became the entry device into Apple’s ecosystem. And while investors had been throwing around the term 'ecosystem' for a long time, Apple had really been making its money from phone upgrades, not really so much from any ecosystem.
However, the problem for Apple soon became that each phone upgrade was really bringing users smaller leaps in technology with each handset, simply because the technology was good enough in each of its latest two or three models.
In fact, arguably, competitors' devices had also become good enough for many consumers. Why pay north of $700 for a phone when the cheaper alternatives could arguably perform just as well (sometimes better?).
So Apple needed a new trick to get consumers wanting to buy its devices, rather than give preference towards seeking out cheaper alternatives in the first instance. So it came up with the idea of building on its iTunes platform by developing a subscription service.
Examples of its subscription services now include: Apple Music, Apple News and Newspapers & magazines, and others. Furthermore, there must be quite a lot of appetite amongst consumers for paying for Apple News, because not only did Apple deem it necessary to go out and acquire Texture (for an undisclosed amount , although deemed immaterial), but more importantly, it is showing strong ambition to get into the 'all-you-can-read' news service, not unlike Netflix's ( NFLX ) all you can binge . Will Apple News become even 10% as successful as Apple Music in getting users to pay for what they were previously used to getting for free? If it does, then Apple would get yet another home run, and its shareholders satisfactorily rewarded.
For now, it is too early to know for sure how successful Apple News will actually become, but there certainly appears to be strong demand for subscribing to its service, and equally important, publishers too are very keen to solidify on this opportunity.
Incidentally, as Alphabet ( GOOGL ) ( GOOG ) highlighted during its latest earnings call , it has set out and collaborated with more than 300 news publishers on its offering, Subscribe with Google, to deliver to end users premium quality journalism.
Moreover, Apple's subscription appears to be growing exponentially. As of Q2 2018 , paid subscriptions had grown from 240 million subscribers, with another 30 million subscribers joining between Q1 2018 and Q2 2018 alone, to break through 270 million paying subscribers.
Further, Apple does not disclose its margins from its subscribers' revenue, but common sense alone dictates that its margins should be far better than those derived from selling hardware alone. Accordingly, Apple reports its subscribers' revenue under its Services segment, and according to Apple's Q2 2018 10-Q , Apple describes how its Services revenue contributes positively towards Apple's gross margins. Moreover, Apple has stated that it has the bold ambition of having its high margin Services segment reach $50 billion by 2021 . However, presently, investors are not being asked to pay for the likelihood that Apple does deliver on its ambitions.

The above table speaks for itself. I have chosen Netflix as a competitor to Apple. Realistically, Netflix is not a competitor to Apple, but I have chosen it because I highlight Netflix’s offering in the article above and also because it goes to show just how far Apple is, from what I deem to be 'bubble' territory. I believe that most reasonable investors can recognize a bubble when they see one, and Apple is very far from that.
Additionally, I like to look at the P/S ratio of Apple and compare its present multiple with that of its previous 5-years’ P/S multiple. Here we can see that investors are truly unimpressed with Apple at present - which really screams of a bargain opportunity to me.
As I have attempted to argue in the article above, Apple should see its margins expand going forward, as it becomes less reliant on selling hardware and more successful at promoting its Services segment.
Takeaway Apple does not seem happy to rest on its laurels. Apple continues to be a growth company, driven and determined and learning new tricks on how to improve its business model. I contend that going forward we should come to see its present valuation of $900 billion as a mirage. That is not to say that the path towards $1.5 trillion (or thereabouts) will be in a straight line, no, on the contrary, it will have many down days, but over time, savvy investors should come to see these as an opportunity to capitalize on.
